name: Fio
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

sources.citation: Good, Jeff. 2013. A (micro-)accretion zone in a remnant zone? Lower Fungom in areal-historical perspective. / Di Carlo, P. & J. Good. 2014. What are we trying to preserve? Diversity, change, and ideology at the edge of the Cameroonian Grassfields. In Austin & Sallabank (eds), Endangered Languages: Beliefs and Ideologies, 231-264. OUP.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Neither paper mentions Fio at all (a full-text search for stress/accent); downloaded only to check for a Fio mention. (Mve et al. 2019 esoterogeny paper also downloaded but has no text layer and was not scanned; it concerns Fang of Lower Fungom.)

sources.citation: Budji Kefen Ivoline. 2015. Spotlight on a Threatened Language: The Fio Language of the Bamenda Grassfields of North western Cameroon. MA thesis (Anthropology), Catholic University of Cameroon (CATUC), Bamenda. 131 pp. Supervisors P. N. Nkwi and P. Di Carlo.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing. Anthropological/sociolinguistic thesis (chapters: theory, literature, methods, Fio people, social organisation, language use). a full-text search for stress/accent finds no 'stress', 'accent', 'tone', 'tonal', 'syllab', 'prosod', 'pitch' or 'intonation'. Only linguistic content is a glossary (pp. iv-v) of ~40 Fio cultural terms in IPA with tone marks. States 'The Fio language is more similar to Beboid languages than to any other subgrouping of Bantoid languages in the area' (p. 90) and 'There are only 8 fluent speakers of Fio' (p. 97); location lat 6°31.256'N, long 10°29.360'E, near…

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.3 languoid record for Fio [fioo1234] and reference records 572960 (Budji 2015: listed by Glottolog as an ethnographic work;socling) and 309782 (Di Carlo 2011: 'mention of Fio').
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Bibliographic only: Glottolog lists exactly two references for Fio, both classed 'a wordlist or less'; no phonology, sketch or grammar exists in its bibliography.

sources.citation: Di Carlo, Pierpaolo. 2011. Lower Fungom linguistic diversity and its historical development: proposals from a multidisciplinary perspective. Africana Linguistica 17: 53-100. DOI 10.3406/aflin.2011.994.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing on Fio phonology. Single mention (p. 82): 'Several sources report that within the village communities of Mbuk, Mungong, Faat, and Fio – all under the Fon of Bum – there are still speakers of the languages used in these villages before the advent of the Alung dynasty and their subsequent absorption into Bum. These languages seem to differ more or less markedly from Bum [bmv] (Lamberty 2002: 3, Nyamnjoh 1997: 10).'

sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Stubs; no linguistic description. The French page supplied the open Dropbox link to the Budji 2015 thesis and the '8 speakers (Ivoline 2015: 103)' figure (the thesis actually gives it on p. 97).

sources.citation: Any future field description of Fio by the University at Buffalo / Jeff Good – Pierpaolo Di Carlo Grassfields projects (Budji's 2015 thesis was NSF-funded through them; no phonological sketch of Fio has been published as of this reading).
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.note: Only a first-hand phonological sketch (even a wordlist with tone marking) could yield a stress/tone statement; none exists in Glottolog, OpenAlex/Crossref author search, or the Buffalo publication page.

sources.citation: Lamberty, Melinda. 2002. A rapid appraisal survey of Bum (Boyo Division, North West Province, Cameroon). SIL International electronic survey report.
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.note: The only survey that treats Fio village (as a Bum community with its own residual language); might contain a short Fio wordlist or a note on its affiliation, but as an RA sociolinguistic survey it almost certainly says nothing about stress. Low value for the catalog.

sources.citation: Brye, Edward & Elizabeth Brye. 2001. Rapid Appraisal and Intelligibility Testing Surveys of the Eastern Beboid Group of Languages (Northwest Province). Yaoundé: SIL International.
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.note: Covers the Eastern Beboid group Fio is assigned to (Cung, Mbuk, Noni etc.); might mention Fio's affiliation, but no phonology or stress expected.

sources.citation: Lamberty, Melinda. 2002. A rapid appraisal / sociolinguistic survey of Bum (Boyo Division, North West Province). SIL International (electronic survey report).
sources.tag: not read: abstract or record only
sources.note: Not opened (sil.org search could not be reached by automated download). Cited by Di Carlo 2011: 3 and Budji 2015 as reporting that Fio is one of six Bum communities whose own language differs from Bum and for whom Bum is a second language; an RA survey, unlikely to describe stress.
